decisions.title: Known mGBA mismatches live in each unit's env file
decisions.why: A unit's input script means ROM plus frames isn't a key, so just unit reads MGBA_HASH and MGBA_WHY from units/NAME.env instead of known-mismatches.tsv (which mgba-diff keeps using).

decisions.title: A unit is stopped and split at ~3 hours, not 90 min
decisions.why: june: units running an hour are fine and not a bad sign; at about 3 hours a unit should have been broken up.

decisions.title: Stay on mGBA 0.10.5; our reset copies its HLE BIOS's
decisions.why: mGBA master (fd9dc5c) passes jsmolka bios 001 but still fails thumb 230 and now arm 522, so no pin change. Machine::new leaves r14=0x08000000 and carry set, as mGBA's HLE resetBase does, so register dumps from reset compare equal; frame hashes unchanged.

decisions.title: Sound is judged against mGBA from a state; GBATEK refill stays
decisions.why: just mgba-audio-diff from frame-100 mGBA states is byte-exact on the 18157 Hz ROM (600 frames) and the 10512 Hz ROM (1000), so the FIFO refill rule (<=16 bytes) never shows. From reset agb's boot runs fast here (no wait states) and music starts 3 buffers early, so compare from a state.

decisions.title: Self-patching IWRAM code: versions seen at recompile time
decisions.why: Rogue's mixer patches its loop per channel (3 templates). gbaa-recompile runs the ROM 1800 frames in the interpreter and compiles each block version seen, guarded by its own bytes; guards are per block. Deterministic, from git; unseen bytes fall back. Fallback 37.8% to 2.2%.

decisions.title: mGBA's 8-bit blend rounding is a known mismatch
decisions.why: Our mGBA build mixes widened 8-bit channels, rounding some blended pixels up a 5-bit step; hardware (GBATEK) and mGBA's 16-bit build don't. We keep the 5-bit mix; units hit by it set MGBA_HASH after proving the swap reproduces mGBA's hash.

decisions.title: Short input scripts are fine; long routes use an existing TAS
decisions.why: june: a checkpoint's input script is a test, so a few presses to reach a screen are fine. Never build a long gameplay route (a TAS) ourselves; if one is needed, use a published TAS (e.g. a TASVideos movie) converted to our input format, and ask june first.

decisions.title: Gamepads read through gilrs; positional default layout
decisions.why: gilrs is pure Rust (no SDL2 dev or cmake), reads evdev so it sees Steam Input's virtual pad in Game Mode, honours SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG, and runs on Windows/macOS. Default: east=A, south=B as on a GBA; ~/.config/gbaa/gamepad.conf rebinds per button

decisions.title: Pad west saves a state, north loads it
decisions.why: The GBA has two face buttons, so west and north are free in the positional layout. They act on the slot last used (1 at first); keyboard Shift+F1-F4 saves, F1-F4 loads. gamepad.conf rebinds save-state and load-state.

decisions.title: Register dumps step to the loop head before printing
decisions.why: Compiled code ends a frame only at a block start; the interpreter after any instruction, so in a busy wait loop (Emerald's WaitForVBlank) the registers matched by luck. gbaa-desktop --regs now steps the interpreter, no IRQs, until a backward branch, in both runs; the frame hash is still taken at frame end.

decisions.title: Rewind is held on R, or the right stick pushed left
decisions.why: Every pad button already has a GBA or front-end job (triggers double L/R; west/north are save states); the right stick's directions were free and the Deck has one. Keyboard R is unbound. Rebind with 'rewind =' in gamepad.conf.

decisions.title: Fix the Groudon regression before the title screen
decisions.why: The title checkpoint (frame 3800) runs through frame 2400, so a drift there would likely make the title unit chase the same bug.

decisions.title: Checkpoints are one check per route, not a unit each
decisions.why: Owner 2026-10-23: a ROM's checkpoints share one input route, so one build checks them all; units are the fixes the first failing checkpoint needs. A ROM can have several routes when paths diverge.

decisions.title: New check and data logic in Rust or TOML, not bash
decisions.why: Owner 2026-10-23, frustrated that agents keep reaching for bash: checkers, input scripts and checkpoint data go in Rust code or declarative files; just recipes stay thin calls.

decisions.title: Route inputs are TOML press tables, not a string
decisions.why: Owner 2026-10-23: each press or run of presses is a [[press]] table (button, at, or from/to/every, optional hold). --input on the CLI keeps its string syntax.

decisions.title: Known mGBA mismatches live on the route's checkpoint
decisions.why: units/*.env became TOML routes ({unit:shared/route-checks}): a checkpoint's mgba_hash and mgba_why sit beside its hash in units/<route>.toml; known-mismatches.tsv stays mgba-diff's.

decisions.title: Netplay: every peer runs every console; lockstep, no rollback
decisions.why: Only inputs cross the network, so the link cable stays exact inside each process (Dolphin's integrated-GBA way). Our targets are turn-based, where 3-6 frames of input delay don't show; rollback waits for a real-time game. docs/research/multiplayer.md.

decisions.title: Lua scripts follow mGBA 0.10.5's API where 0.11-dev differs
decisions.why: 0.10.5 is the latest mGBA release, so scripts in the wild target it. getGameCode differs (AGB-BPEE vs BPEE) and each pokemon.lua recognises Emerald only in its own format (probe in docs/research/lua-scripting.md). Take 0.11-dev's additions only where they don't clash.

decisions.title: Lua runs on mlua with vendored PUC Lua 5.4, outside runtime
decisions.why: mGBA builds against Lua 5.4 and its scripts use 5.3+ syntax (bit operators) that LuaJIT and Luau can't parse; piccolo lacks most of the standard library. Vendored builds need only a C compiler on Linux, macOS, Windows. runtime stays no_std, so Lua lives in a desktop-side crate.

decisions.title: Multiplayer: which kind of linking should be built first: Cable first: trades and battles with friends
decisions.why: builds the plan as filed: link hub, local two-player window, netplay core, relay server, then june plays a friend. Wireless and shared overworld stay later research
decisions.question: q/multiplayer-kind-linking-built-first

decisions.title: Multiplayer: where should the server run: A machine of june's that is always on
decisions.why: Start the relay as a separate program (later optionally built into the game). june wants it to know nothing about the game: the same server works for any game, any console. Build a quick prototype first to find out if that holds. Which always-on machine: not named yet, ask june when the relay unit needs it.
decisions.question: q/multiplayer-where-server-run

decisions.title: What should the in-game menus be built on: winit + egui (OpenGL)
decisions.why: Changed by june (2026-10-24): egui yes, but SDL3 (the sdl3 crate, vhspace/sdl3-rs) instead of winit for the window and graphics layer, and for gamepads (button labels, the Deck's controller, Steam Input), replacing gilrs; egui drawn through SDL's renderer (Vulkan/Metal/D3D as SDL picks), not OpenGL. The glue from egui to the SDL renderer may be ours to write. Audio (cpal or SDL's) is the implementer's call, say why. egui's look is ours to style; june has no opinion on egui details. Accessibility through AccessKit (AT-SPI on Linux) is wanted later, not now.
decisions.question: q/game-menus-built

decisions.title: Menus in egui, drawn through SDL3; SDL3 for window, graphics and pads
decisions.why: june, 2026-10-24: SDL3 (sdl3 crate, vhspace/sdl3-rs) for the window and graphics layer instead of winit, and for gamepads (button labels, the Deck's controller, Steam Input) in place of gilrs; egui for the menus and later the Lua console, drawn through SDL's renderer (Vulkan/Metal/D3D as SDL picks), not OpenGL. The egui-to-SDL-renderer glue may be ours to write. Audio stays cpal unless the implementer shows SDL's is better. egui's styling is ours to settle. Accessibility via AccessKit later, not now. Research: docs/research/ui-library.md.

decisions.title: How much may a Lua script do on your machine: Limited, with a per-script full-access switch
decisions.why: scripts can only touch files in their own folder and talk to this machine; Ironmon's tracking works at once, and its updater and new-run automation work once you flip its switch (remembered)

decisions.why: nothing to build; a script that asks gets a warning

decisions.title: Ctrl+Q quits the window; Escape never does
decisions.why: Steam's desktop controller layout sends Escape for the Deck's B, and holding B (running in Pokémon) is common, so even Escape held would quit by accident. Escape only closes the menu; quit by Ctrl+Q, the menu's Quit, the window's close button or Steam's Exit game.

decisions.title: Pad A and B follow the buttons' labels
decisions.why: june, play test 2026-10-23: the GBA-positional default (A east, B south) felt wrong; the button labelled A should press GBA A. Default a = label-a, b = label-b: south/east on Xbox pads and the Deck, east/south on Nintendo pads. gilrs was since replaced by SDL3.

decisions.title: Windows only in a private cu session, never june's screen
decisions.why: june, 2026-10-24: a lane opened windows on june's real desktop. Any run that opens a window (gbaa-desktop without --headless, SDL, fullscreen or resize checks) goes in a private headless KWin via the cu CLI (cu session; linux-computer-use skill). Prefer --headless where it suffices.

decisions.title: Structured code: interpret resumes, or keep a second body: One structured body; resumes interpreted, then won back
decisions.why: One body, but the runtime changes come first and change: calls settled in place (wider), IRQs in the tick, and the guest on its own stack so the frame end doesn't unwind. Spike: 1 resume a frame, 99.2% compiled, hashes exact. Design doc steps 5-8.
decisions.question: q/structured-code-interpret-resumes-second

decisions.title: Stop unwinding: guest stack, then one structured body
decisions.why: june, 2026-10-24: resumes are made rare rather than interpreted. Before the emitter: calls settled in place (any key other than the return site), IRQs and halts in the tick, and the guest on its own stack so the frame end pauses it. Two bodies, async codegen and nightly coroutines rejected: docs/structured-codegen-design.md steps 5-8.

decisions.title: How should we get two Emerald saves at a Pokemon Center: Craft them

decisions.title: Scripts load into a running game: start not fired
decisions.why: mGBA 0.10.5 has no --script flag; its scripting window loads a script either before a game (emu nil, then start and reset fire) or into a running one (emu set, nothing fires). We load with emu set, the way the probe ran pokemon.lua and Ironmon; firing start too made idiomatic scripts set up twice.

decisions.title: Multiplayer: vanilla link by default, a per-game mod when vanilla can't deliver
decisions.why: june 2026-10-26. Vanilla (emulate the cable, sync inputs, every peer runs every console) is the default: no per-game work, exact, works for any game, enough for turn-based or menu-driven link play (Emerald trades and battles). Mod a game's netcode when the feature doesn't exist in the game (shared overworld, drop-in, >4 players) or its real-time link protocol can't survive internet latency even with rollback. Where the game already ships a networking mod (Emerald Rogue's Rogue Assistant blobs), implement its other end. Applied: Emerald trades/battles vanilla; Rogue co-op mod side; Kirby co-op vanilla with rollback first, mod only if it feels bad; shared overworld mod only. june's long-term aim is the modded route for good multiplayer.

decisions.title: Online play with a friend: where does the server run: A small rented VPS

decisions.title: Mod copies live in mods/<game>/ in this private repo
decisions.why: Decision 2 says a mod is ordinary Rust in git once cut; a mod is a few dozen translated functions, like the committed Emerald snapshots, and the repo is private. Never in a public repo. docs/mod-view-design.md 'A mod copy'.

decisions.title: Mod view prints pret's file:line, never pret's C text
decisions.why: The source map holds only addresses, names, sizes, paths and C types as text (decision 2's legality line). file:line lets a reader with pokeemerald open the line; copying C source into generated output is avoided. docs/mod-view-design.md 'The readable form'.

decisions.title: Source map file is the ELF's object name; dup names need two files
decisions.why: STT_FILE names objects (main.o) and 69 of 893 stems match no single source file, so file is the object name; a source path waits for DWARF. One map file may give one name to two addresses only when their files differ (pret's statics); else the loader refuses.

decisions.title: Mod view prints maintainable Rust close to pret's C
decisions.why: june 2026-10-26: the readable form aims at decompiled, maintainable Rust, not translated asm with names. Target, for ClearBattleMonForms: fn clear_battle_mon_forms(g: &mut Game) { for i in (0..4).rev() { g.battle_mon_forms[i] = 0; } }. Timing and flags hidden in macros, exact still. Not perfect pret C; maintainable is the bar. pret's C (and its DWARF types) is the oracle.

decisions.title: May readable Rust leave dead scratch registers at a return: Allow registers dead at every return site to differ
decisions.why: The printer drops those syncs, so bodies get about a third shorter. Needs an interprocedural liveness proof, and fn-diff compares only live state at returns. The Emerald route same-states check still runs.
decisions.question: q/may-readable-rust-leave-dead

decisions.title: How should a headless lane get SSH onto your Deck: You approve the check now and then

decisions.title: Asset overrides key on ROM address, served at the load
decisions.why: gbaa owns the BIOS decompressors and DMA, so it sees each load's ROM source: exact, one lookup a load, and names match the manifest and source map. Content-hash keys (Dolphin, PPSSPP) suit emulators that only see VRAM. docs/asset-extraction-design.md, Overrides.

decisions.title: Naming agents: Sonnet 5.5 via claude -p, with no tools
decisions.why: The naming loop's agent is claude -p --tools '' --safe-mode from an empty /tmp folder, so it can't read pret's source on disk and only the prompt reaches it; Sonnet 5.5 for cost (about $14 list per 300-function round). naming ask --model changes it.

decisions.title: Readable sync blocks are the exit macro's trailing argument
decisions.why: A macro_rules! per exit at the top of the function can't name the block's let-bound values: macro hygiene resolves locals where the macro is defined. So each exit's sync (regs!) is a trailing { } argument of tick!/call!/ret!, after the body's C lines. docs/mod-view-design.md, under {unit:mod/readable-lowering}.

decisions.title: Netplay is rollback over plain UDP; lockstep and QUIC parked
decisions.why: june (2026-10-27), after playing both: lockstep freezes at every late input, and its QUIC relay doesn't work through fly.io. Rollback (--rollback, gbaa-server's plain-UDP rooms on 7374) is what netplay work builds on; lockstep stays in the code, unchanged, but gets no more work unless june says.

decisions.title: Netplay is rollback over plain UDP; lockstep and QUIC parked
decisions.why: june (2026-10-27), after playing both over fly.io: lockstep freezes at every late input, and its QUIC relay doesn't work through fly. Every peer still runs every console and only inputs cross the wire, but by rollback (--rollback, gbaa-server's plain-UDP rooms on 7374, netplay::rollback). Lockstep stays in the code, unchanged, and gets no more work unless june says.

decisions.title: Netplay: every peer runs every console, by rollback
decisions.why: june (2026-10-27) parked lockstep and QUIC ({d:netplay-is-rollback-over-plain-udp-lockstep-and-2}): only inputs cross the network and every peer runs every console, as before, but by rollback over plain UDP, not lockstep. Kirby's real-time co-op showed lockstep's freezes; rollback is for turn-based games too.

decisions.title: Netplay: zero input delay; others may teleport
decisions.why: june (2026-10-27): a press reaches your own console on the next frame, every game, turn-based too; other players may teleport. Input delay is never the fix for a bad connection or slow machine: speed is (recompiled netplay, no drawing on re-runs). Rollback is the desktop default at delay 0, lockstep behind --lockstep. The window is 300 frames (5 s), not Slippi's 7: don't freeze over a late input. Build, play, find what's bad, then fix it.

decisions.title: Netplay: lockstep and QUIC are removed, not parked
decisions.why: june (2026-10-27): rip lockstep and QUIC out. Rollback over plain UDP at delay 0 is the only netplay ({d:netplay-zero-input-delay-others-may-teleport}). Every peer still runs every console and only inputs cross the wire.

decisions.why: june played instant Kirby and can't tell it apart, finds it more responsive. mGBA stays the oracle through exact. A new check that recompiles must pass --timing exact (docs/research/mod-view-without-timing.md).

decisions.title: The interpreter plays instant too; checks pin it exact
decisions.why: june, 2026-10-31: gbaa-desktop on a ROM defaults to --timing instant like play builds; a recompiled build's fallback and --interp follow the build's own timing; every check that runs gbaa-desktop or a build passes --timing exact (route-check --args prints it); gbaa-interp stays exact. decisions.title: A lost mod call reruns its block from a guest-RAM record
decisions.why: A call a mod adds has no ROM code to resume at and its Rust frame can't be rebuilt (that'd be a state machine). Its record (r0-r14, CPSR, the block's key) sits below the callee's stack, so after a load, rewind or unwind the guest goes on where the block began: stock code, or the mod from its top. docs/mod-view-design.md, 'A call a mod adds'.

decisions.title: Modded builds are plain Rust programs: no save states, rewind or rollback

Unmodded builds keep save states, rewind, rollback, mGBA states and exact checks, with real ROM addresses in their state. Modded builds are fully native Rust using ordinary memory, no GBA memory block, and get none of those. No middle ground for now. The lost-mod-call rerun from a guest-RAM record is unsound under rollback and not needed. docs/decisions.md, decision 2.

decisions.title: The native check skips a replaced library's state by name

A literal lift needs no list; the recogniser should emit it.

decisions.title: The native check takes the lowest sp from the play build's interpreter
decisions.why: From {unit:native/oracle}: compiled code never writes a block's lowest sp to r13 (balanced push/pop are folded), so noting r13 writes saw 0x03007e9c where the stack reached 0x03007e94. route-check --native runs the play build again with --interp (Machine::low_sp, after every instruction), whose records must equal the compiled run's.

decisions.title: Stage A passes r0-r3 in and out of every function; the summaries mark holes
decisions.why: From Stage-A lifter ({unit:native/lift-stage-a}): each lifted function keeps r4-r11, lr and NZCV in its own Rust locals, so a callee can't change its caller's and fn(g, sp, [r0..r3]) -> [r0..r3] is exact for any AAPCS callee. The summaries' proof fails on 47-50 of each agb program's ~110 functions for analysis reasons (indirect calls, callees that never return); a summary that returns r4-r11 or sp changed is a hard hole, the rest are listed soft. Fewer parameters from the summaries is stage B's.

decisions.title: Stage A keeps the guest stack as IWRAM bytes, sp a parameter
decisions.why: From Stage-A lifter ({unit:native/lift-stage-a}): agb code passes addresses of stack values everywhere, so frames as Rust locals need section 1's escape analysis (stage B). The frames stay at the guest's addresses (the native check skips the stack from the lowest sp); Game::sp is the sp at the last wait, where an IRQ handler that switches to system mode puts its frames.

decisions.title: Stage-A function pointers are ROM keys; no dense IDs until stage B
decisions.why: From Stage-A lifter ({unit:native/lift-stage-a}): a literal lift loads function pointers from ROM bytes and RAM (agb's vtables and closures), so it can't renumber them; FnRef IDs are the function's key (address, Thumb bit) in every stage-A build, as --fn-ids rom says. Dense IDs need the points-to facts of stage B.

decisions.title: The lifter decodes discovery's gaps itself and lists them
decisions.why: From Stage-A lifter ({unit:native/lift-stage-a}): a jump into ROM where discovery has no code (a bl's second half taken for a literal pool, a scanned fragment stopped short) falls to the interpreter in the play build but would be a hard hole natively. gbaa-lift decodes from each such target until known code, joins split bl halves, repeats until none are left, and lists the targets in its report (22, 5 and 143 on the three agb programs). Fixing discovery would make it a no-op.

decisions.title: Recognised agb is replaced by hand-written Rust over Hw
decisions.why: From stage-B planning (docs/native-stage-b.md, piece 2): the real agb crate targets the GBA (memory-mapped I/O, asm!) and doesn't build for the host, so a recognised agb or core function becomes hand-written Rust kept once per agb version, keyed by symbol, over runtime::hw and the prelude. Leaves (panic path, mem*, division, critical sections) keep RAM byte for byte so the native check needs no skips; agb's stateful runtime (interrupt list, vblank, entry) gets a skip list the lifter generates.

decisions.title: Stage-B checks are bars in one committed file, only lowered
decisions.why: From stage-B planning: every stage-B unit is checked by lift-check staying green plus a metric moving. gbaa-lift prints the metrics and --bars fails over a maximum in one committed TOML; each unit lowers the bars it names. Raising a bar to pass is changing the oracle: ask june. Checks in Rust/TOML, not bash (june's preference).

decisions.title: agb's allocator stays lifted until pointers are typed
decisions.why: From stage-B planning: agb's heap holds the program's own objects (closures, Vecs) whose pointers are guest addresses in stage A. Replacing the allocator before Ref<T> would move them and break every pointer, so lib-agb-runtime leaves it lifted and ref-pointers takes it up.

decisions.title: Shortcut fixes ship with an agb test program and a control
decisions.why: From stage-B planning: the fallthrough and IRQ-hold shortcuts pass on the three agb programs, so a fix there would be checked by nothing. Each fix writes a small agb program of ours that hits the case (global_asm! where needed), adds it to lift-check, and keeps the old behaviour behind a flag that must fail the check. Same for stack locals, since the native check skips the stack.

decisions.title: Indirect calls pass r0-r3 until their callee sets are known
decisions.why: From stage-B planning, settling what {unit:native/summaries} left open: all four registers is sound and is what stage A does; computing callee sets needs the points-to the dense FnRef IDs build anyway. So parameters-from-summaries keeps all four at indirect calls, and indirect-call-args then passes the union of a complete callee set's summaries (an incomplete set keeps all four).

decisions.title: Stage-B sprint 2026-11-01: one unit at a time, Metroid track third

decisions.title: A bar may rise only when accesses move out of computed_unknown
decisions.why: Bars only go down, but better analysis moves accesses from load/store_computed_unknown into a region's computed_<region> count, which would push that region's bar up. A unit may raise a computed_<region> bar by no more than the same direction's computed_unknown bar drops, with the moved count stated in its evidence; the total of computed loads (and of stores) never rises. Any other raise still goes to june.

decisions.title: A fall into another function goes through its extended entry, not a copy of its blocks
decisions.why: From {unit:native/lift-fallthrough}: every lifted function is x_<key>(g, Regs) with r0-r14 and NZCV, f_<key> a one-line call into it; a fall, jump or call-return into another function's entry passes every register and flag. Copying blocks duplicates code (agb programs have ~13 falls each into library code) and chains; the extended entry cost no lines (the old five-line header became three). Stand-ins and call_fn tail jumps still use the plain entry.

decisions.title: Gap decoding stops after a bl whose return site is a known literal pool
decisions.why: From {unit:native/lift-fallthrough}: force_code decoded past agb qrcodegen's panic bl into its pool, an undefined instruction (hard hole) in the new program's layout. Such a bl can't return (it would run data). Dropped pool-as-code from every lift (mosaic-modes gap targets 143 -> 24, lines 74,432 -> 51,309); native check still green on all four programs; bars lowered.

decisions.title: The native-timing play build takes an IRQ the I bit held as soon as an msr clears I
decisions.why: From {unit:native/lift-irq-hold}: at --timing native the play build opened its IRQ window only where time passed, so an IRQ held by I in a critical section waited past the msr to the next wait; mGBA takes it at the msr (agb/native-irq-hold drew c2-c0 = 0 at native, 1 in mGBA). tick_native now opens the window when I is clear and an IRQ the last sync found is still pending; a control msr ends a compiled block, so compiled code and the interpreter take it at the same instruction. Native timing at frame 601 now hashes as mGBA (abc7ac7a22ed22b3). IME has the same shape and is left as is (both builds agree; only a test against mGBA would see it).

decisions.title: agb/native-irq-hold's route stops at frame 601, not 600
decisions.why: From {unit:native/lift-irq-hold}: a pixel lands about every frame and a half, and at frame 600 our exact interpreter has drawn one more than mGBA (frame 599's picture is mGBA's 600); at 598, 601 and 610 they agree. The checkpoint must be mGBA's hash, so the route is units/native-irq-hold-601.toml.

decisions.title: The lift's line count leaves out the hand-written prelude, which has its own bar
decisions.why: From {unit:native/lift-irq-hold} (owner's call, via the parent session): the prelude (crates/codegen/src/native/prelude.rs) is hand-written runtime code in every lifted crate, not lifted output, so it shouldn't share a bar with what the lifter makes. lines now counts everything the lift writes but the prelude (bars: the old values less the old 414-line prelude; still only lowered); lines_prelude counts the prelude (bar 439 after this unit's +25). lines_prelude may rise when a unit adds hand-written prelude code, if the unit's evidence says how many lines and why; lines still only goes down.

decisions.title: A native direct-sound program stands for the card's bios-sound
decisions.why: From {unit:native/hw-sound}: the card asked for a native bios-sound playing direct sound by timer and DMA, but agb/bios-sound only calls the BIOS sound driver's no-op stubs and plays nothing. agb/direct-sound (new) plays both FIFOs from IWRAM double buffers swapped by a cascaded timer's IRQ (agb's mixer's shape), matches mGBA's sound for 299 frames, and its native port passes route-check --native with samples equal every frame; psg-square covers FIFO A by DMA1 on timer 0 with the PSG.

decisions.title: Native timing releases an IRQ only when IME goes 0 to 1
decisions.why: On the hardware a pending IRQ is taken the moment IME is set again. The native-timing play build acts on that write alone (event IME_ON), not on any IE/IF change, so an IRQ requested between time points with IME on (a DMA end) still waits for the next time point, as the native library does. The recompiler at native timing ends a block after a store that folds to IME, so compiled code and interpreter take it at the same instruction; an unfolded IME store still ticks at its block end.

decisions.title: Netplay waits 8 s for a silent peer before it has left

The owner may prefer shorter.

decisions.title: A constant jump to a RAM copy's function is resolved
decisions.why: From Discover code past m4a's and Nightmare's copy sources ({unit:native/copy-tail-discovery}): a jump to one constant RAM address (m4a's SoundMain into its IWRAM copy, Minish Cap's ROM-to-IWRAM veneers) is Recovery's JumpRes::Ram. It is no more a hole than a constant call: the hole report doesn't count it where an overlay discovered a function at the target, and the lifter jumps to that function (a hole if none is there). Hard total over the corpus 106 to 103. Code discovery then finds that hides a real hole counts it: Nightmare's resume bx r1 (0x08000254) takes it 9 to 10, covered by its task switcher's stand-in.

decisions.title: A networked adapter lists only the hosts the server says are open

decisions.title: A networked adapter keeps the 3 s host memory
decisions.why: Rerun of the latency sweep (multiplayer.md, 'The radio on the server'): without HEARD_FOR, 100 and 120 ms each way lost BOB's offer from ALICE's board; with it 0-200 ms all trade. Cost: a first Connect to a stale host ID is refused and retried (~100 frames). --heard-ms 0 turns it off.

decisions.title: Lift bars: agents may raise a count, with the cause named
decisions.why: june, 2026-11-12. The bars in crates/codegen/lift-check.toml measure how plain the lifted code is; they are not the correctness check. Correctness stays june's: the native check (the lifted build draws its route's frames as the interpreter does), hard_holes and the planted controls never loosen without her. Any other bar may be raised by the unit's own session, with no question, when the native check stays green and the unit's evidence gives each raised bar, its old and new value, and the cause (the old value was unsound or an accident, or counts moved between categories). The loop's review judges that explanation. Each raise is also recorded with 'just tracker decide --for-run', so the morning report shows it. Still ask june when the bar that would rise is the metric the unit's own done-when says must fall, or when a rise is large and its cause isn't found. Replaces 'only lowered': six raise questions in a week, the first five all answered yes, each holding finished work for hours.
